changesets.headline: a month position past the end of a Gregorian-aligned calendar's year constrains to that year's last month in calendarMonthFromYearMonth and useCalendarDays, instead of returning a NaN CalendarMonth and laying out the next year's January (#10461)

Declare renderer-owned DOM boundaries so decorator overlays mount outside managed content without changing safe inline hosting. RichTextEditor also mirrors its `dir` prop onto the wrapper around the editable surface, so the editing surface and its content blocks, the placeholder, UI rendered through `plugins`, and relocated overlays follow `dir`; the editing surface previously kept the surrounding direction.

On Android, text follows the reader's system font scale in every theme with no setup, in browsers that report `env(preferred-text-scale)` (verified on Chromium and on Chrome stable). The root `Theme` reads `env(preferred-text-scale)` and scales every font size by it, as it already follows Dynamic Type on iPhone. Before, the system font scale reached Astryx text only when the page added `<meta name="text-scale" content="scale">`. A page with `content="scale"` keeps working as it did: its root font size carries the scale, and the root `Theme` adds none. Browsers without either see no change. `astryx docs typography/type-scale` describes it.

Motion: in WebKit on Linux, the last frame of an `animatedLayout` change shows where each motion ends once a frame has drawn the motion near its end. Under load, that frame, and every frame of a long task over its end, could show a glide, an exit's fade or an indicator's turn part of the way through: a collapsing `TreeList` drew the rows below 44 px back, its leaving rows half faded and its chevron mid-turn. A long task that starts before that frame, or a motion near its end only at its last keyframe, can still show it. At normal speed the motion is unchanged.
Motion: a Switch's value change mid-travel keeps the thumb's running speed. A rebase toward the new rest shifts the curve whole.
`astryx discover` lists the Lab DialogHeroHeaderShowcase template from `@astryxdesign/lab`. (#4182)
`astryx discover` lists the Lab DialogHeroHeader component from `@astryxdesign/lab`. (#4182)

Avatar: initials are drawn as generated content with empty alternative text instead of text, so axe's Label in Name check (`label-content-name-mismatch`) no longer flags a link or button avatar that shows initials. The accessible name, the name tooltip and the initials' appearance are unchanged.

BottomSheet: at rest, a sheet's content starts below the grab bar whatever its `padding`, so the first line is no longer drawn through the bar's fade. The block-start inset is never less than the bar's height (`--spacing-6`): the band under the bar is not padding a child escapes, so a lone `Section` starts below the bar too; scrolled content still passes beneath it. A sheet at the default padding starts its content 8 px lower, one with `padding={0}` starts it below the bar, and one whose only child is a `Section` starts that Section 24 px lower and grows by the same amount. Core's own `padding={0}` sheets (the touch date and time pickers, the DropdownMenu and ContextMenu sheets, and the PowerSearch and Tokenizer sheets) no longer reserve that band themselves, so the pickers, PowerSearch and Tokenizer look the same and a menu's first row sits 8 px lower. The CLI's `table-filter` and `table-inbox` page templates drop their own band too, so it is not doubled.

Under reduced motion, a `BottomSheet` that a finger's swipe dismisses fades out where the finger left it. Before, it jumped back to its open position in one frame and faded from there. With motion, the next open after such a swipe rises from below the screen again, instead of starting where the finger left the sheet.

BottomSheet: a drag reads its release velocity from Core's velocity tracker, on each event's own timestamp, also when a touch drag starts on the sheet's content. The release depends on the last two moves, so a move that reaches the page late earlier in a flick no longer slows the flick. A hold weighs on the first move after it, as iOS's filter does. Two rules differ from iOS: a finger that holds still for more than 40 ms before the lift releases nothing in motion, and a release needs two moves.
A stacked `BottomSheet` whose close waits in a suspended transition takes over the dim when the sheet beneath it closes, so the page behind it stays dimmed.

BottomSheet: an open sheet that renders again no longer reads the viewport height. It keeps the viewport height that its `resize` listener reads, so a tap that renders the sheet again forces no style recalculation or layout in React's commit. The sheet's height, reserve and detents are unchanged.

A swizzled copy can now compile as Astryx source in the Babel, PostCSS, and Vite integrations. Every module under a folder that holds an `astryx-swizzle.json` marker gets the library class prefix and lands in `@layer astryx-base`, below `astryx-theme`, so a theme's component overrides reach it. `astryx swizzle` does not write the marker yet: add the file to the swizzle output folder. Under webpack, `withAstryx()` rebuilds a cached copy when its marker appears or disappears. Turbopack builds do not read the marker yet. No API changes.
Butter's buttons take inline padding only and use `Button`'s own block padding. Their height is unchanged.

Button: disabled buttons no longer render the native `disabled` attribute. They stay focusable in keyboard tab order, keep focus when they become disabled while focused (a link Button, which becomes a `<button>` when disabled, still moves focus), and expose `aria-disabled="true"`. All activation paths (mouse clicks, Enter, Space) and clickAction/onClick callbacks remain blocked without losing focus to the document body. A disabled named submit Button withholds its name so `new FormData(form, submitter)` omits its value (FR3). A ButtonGroup whose members are all disabled (whether on the group or individually) keeps its one Tab stop instead of dropping out of the Tab order or giving every member its own stop, and Carousel's hidden scroll buttons are never Tab stops. This meets AST-085 FR1–FR3, FR6 and FR7, and FR4 for every Button that is not a link. Tests that assert `toBeDisabled()` or `:disabled` should query `[aria-disabled="true"]` instead.

A labelled `Button` grows with its label when the text size grows: its height is its size, or one line of its label when that is taller, so the label stays inside the button. At the default text size Buttons render exactly as before, a caller's `height` still applies, and icon-only buttons keep their fixed square.

`Calendar` day buttons grow with their numbers when the person's text size grows, such as a larger browser default font size. Their size is now a minimum, so a day's number stays inside its own tap target and a tap no longer lands on the day below. At the default text size nothing changes.

Under snap paging (`hasSnap={useSnapPaging()}`), Carousel's edge buttons and `handleRef`'s `scrollNext`, `scrollPrev` and `scrollTo` move the row through the paging, also from rest. A touch that catches such a move now leaves the row on a page, as a flick's settle does. On iOS a still touch used to stop the browser's smooth scroll between two items.

Under snap paging (`hasSnap={useSnapPaging()}`), Carousel's edge scroll buttons and edge fades follow the row as it moves. They change in the frame where it leaves an edge. A flick used to leave them as they were until the settle ended and the row went back to native scrolling, so the start button came back about half a second after the row had visibly left the start.

ChatComposerInput: composing with an input method (for example Japanese or Chinese) right after picking a mention, inserting a token, or inserting text after a token now commits only the composed text. The composer places its caret inside the trailing text, not on an element boundary, so the first raw letter of the composition is no longer committed. Right after a mention pick, one Backspace now removes the mention with its space, and no stray line break is left.
Internal: a ChatComposerInput source comment that restated the code is removed. No change to behavior or output.

ChatLayout's scroll-to-bottom button now appears when `scrollRef` names the document's scroller and the reader scrolls the page up. The stream scroll also stops following there, so a streaming reply no longer pulls that reader back to the newest message.

ChatLayout with a `scrollRef` now rests the newest message above the fixed composer dock at the scroll's end. The message area's end padding holds the dock's height and follows it as the composer grows.

ChatLayout keeps its composer on top of the software keyboard where the visual viewport shrinks for it, instead of leaving it underneath until the browser scrolls the whole page. In Chrome on Android the dock rides Gboard's measured slides up and down, in step with the keyboard. In Safari on iOS (in the browser and as a home-screen app) and in Firefox for Android, it moves above the keyboard once the browser reports it. Where a page sets `interactive-widget=resizes-content`, Chrome shrinks the page for the keyboard itself and the composer stays above it without moving. A conversation at its newest message stays there, and the rest of the transcript can still be scrolled above the composer. On a touch screen, in a top-level page, every way into the composer's text (a tap, the keyboard's previous and next buttons, Tab, the input's `focus()`) reaches it without the page scrolling; under a mouse or inside an iframe the browser's own focus applies. In a top-level page on a touch screen, the composer's wrapper (without the scroll-to-bottom button) is a group with no name. When the keyboard's Done ends typing, focus rests there (it is no tab stop), so the next tap or Tab starts from the composer; it shows the focus ring after keyboard input only. A tap that focuses the composer still raises its click once. Under a mouse or inside an iframe, the wrapper is a plain container. Under Reduce Motion the composer never travels with Gboard: it cross-fades to its place above the keyboard. Under a mouse, with no software keyboard, nothing changes. The browser-support guide's section on the on-screen keyboard covers ChatLayout's composer.
`useChatStreamScroll`'s `scrollToMessage` now puts the message at the top of the viewport when the scroller is the page itself. It landed off by the page's own scroll.
`discover` lists the Lab ChatVirtualizer among the official `@astryxdesign/lab` components.

Adds the English default name of the Lab ChatVirtualizer's own scroll container (`@astryx.chatVirtualizer.label`, "Messages"). It is a Lab string shipped in Core's locale file; it adds no public API to `@astryxdesign/core`.
`astryx discover` lists the experimental TabBar and TabBarItem components from `@astryxdesign/lab`.
`integration check` and `experimental icon new-set` follow `export const X = Y` to where `Y` is declared: an icon-set theme map or icon export written that way is now checked and recorded.
Internal: doctor.mjs and template.mjs are formatted with Prettier. No change to any command's output.
`astryx` lists a `create…` factory documented as a hook, such as `createReorderable`, with the hooks.
Internal: the icon-set export reader reuses the shared top-level helper, and a source comment on look refreshes is shorter. No change to any command's output.

Icon sets: when a wrapped library ships no license file, `integration check` on an icon set, `experimental icon new-set --from`, and a refresh name the NOTICE file to add and where, and the icon-sets guide lists the file names that count. A refresh from a library root moves icons added one file at a time from that library to the root import, keeping their ids, exports, map entries, variants, and words, and the receipt lists them under `moved`. Each keeps that id and export on every later refresh, and refreshing again changes nothing. A refresh keeps an id you chose that is not a spelling of the library name (`dismiss` for `XIcon`), also for an icon that already reads the root; it renames only an id the current rule spells differently. A library icon whose id or name a moved icon already has is left out. An icon whose root export another icon of the set already reads stays on its own import, and the receipt says why. A variant from another file of the package, such as a solid look, stays on its own import, and every export the refresh does not write again stays in the generated module. A `LICENSE` directory counts as a license notice in neither the receipt nor the check.

Icon sets: wrapping a large icon library that names its looks in its exports works in seconds and gives one icon per glyph. Only the experimental icon commands, the icon-set guide, and `integration check` on an icon set change.
changesets.body:
- **Large libraries.** `experimental icon new-set --from` reads a library of 20,000 exports in about ten seconds instead of minutes, and in text mode says on stderr that it is reading and what it found. `iconNewSet` and `iconAdd` report reading progress for large modules through the shared `logger` (stderr, text mode only); called directly, they stay silent until `logger.setSilent(false)`.
- **Libraries of looks.** A library whose export names end in style, size and weight words (`XOutline24WGHT500Icon`), never direction words like `Up` and `Down`, gives one icon per glyph, named `x` (`XIcon`), in the look the set's default variant names, else the library's usual default; suggestions and `add` name icons by glyph, `add --variant filled --all` picks each glyph's filled look, a refresh keeps every icon an earlier release wrapped, and a refresh with a new `--default-variant` moves each glyph to that look. Every command that records the default variant takes it from the look each icon's export draws, refuses a look word the library does not have, and never adds a second export of an icon.
- **Variants on an existing set.** `experimental icon new-set <set> --variants outline,filled` without `--from` declares variants (a set with icons keeps its default variant, or, with none declared, takes the look its icons draw; a set whose library's export names name no looks keeps it on a refresh too, refuses `--variants` that leave it out, and the refusal names the `add --variant` run that adds the other look), and `--display-name` and `--description` rewrite the descriptor, in place; `add --variant` names an undeclared variant with that command.
- **Commands that run as printed.** Every command `new-set`, `add` and `map` print names the set, with `--set` where the command takes it; the commands `add` lists repeat `--default` and `--id`; `--new-definition` and `new-definition` take kebab-case as the definitions list shows it, and an unknown `--definition` suggests a name the next command takes.
- **Search.** `experimental icon star` no longer offers `start`, a plural matches its singular, `go home` finds the icon mapped to `home`, and a letter or two never matches inside a word.
- **Checks.** A set's own definitions pass `integration check --strict`, and the generated module and its declaration file pass after a formatter rewrites them.
- **Theme icons.** Each `themeIcons` entry is sized to its box by CSS, so a component that writes its own size attributes still fills the theme's icon box.

changesets.headline: Comments, a codemod note and the grouped-table template's sample data no longer use internal-format identifiers.

Internal: the doc importers import each doc file through one small module that the CLI's own test project loads natively, so its tests no longer time out on a busy machine. No change to any command's output.

`astryx experimental render` matches `compilerOptions.paths` keys and targets by TypeScript's rules, from the project's own tsconfig.json or jsconfig.json (a config it `extends` is not read). Newly, a `*` may sit anywhere in a key or a target (`"theme-*-x"`, `"./icons/icon-*"`), and a key's targets are tried in order, so a module, stylesheet, image or JSON file under a later target is found; `--reverse` puts a file back under the target its sent path names (the one whose folders match the most of the path above the file, a target with text before its `*` included), else under the first target. Only bare specifiers are matched, an import whose targets do not exist resolves as a package, and a catch-all `"*"` key never turns a missing package into a path error. A module the page loads from outside its own files and outside `node_modules` (a sibling package's source, say) resolves a bare import through the same aliases first, as the page's own files and TypeScript do, so the page and that module load one copy of a package; an import no alias places resolves as a package, so an installed package that a prefix key also names (`"@scope/*"` and `@scope/realpkg`) still loads. `--reverse` of a rendered file that lost its embedded source on the way (and has no Astryx components to rebuild from) now fails with `ERR_RENDER_SOURCE_DAMAGED`, saying so, instead of `ERR_RENDER_NOT_ASTRYX`.

`astryx swizzle --list` no longer lists Core's shared folders (`animator`, `gestures`, `i18n`, `internal`, `keyboard`, `motion`, `privateAttributes`, `__tests__`) as components. A copy of `gestures` imports `@astryxdesign/core/motion`, which the core package does not export.

`astryx component` prints a theme warning as one line: control and format characters in the configured `astryx.theme` value or the generated theme record print as `�`, so a newline or an escape sequence in a checkout cannot rewrite the terminal.

`astryx docs <topic>` reads a topic authored as `.doc.ts` from an installed integration on every supported Node, and from a linked integration below Node 22.18. Topic and docs-tree files now load `.ts` through the same TypeScript loader as component docs, where a plain import failed under `node_modules` ("Stripping types is currently unsupported") and below Node 22.18 ("Unknown file extension .ts"). `astryx search` also reads an installed `.doc.ts` component doc, so it finds the component by its keywords, shows its description, and lists a family's members. `.doc.mjs` topics load as before.
CommandPalette stays open with no results when a search or bootstrap request rejects

The source header of `Layout/containerCorners.stylex.ts` (shipped in the package) now says that the `--container-corner-*` variables Card and Dialog set are in `astryx.css`, undocumented, and read only by Table and List; it had said they stay out of public API.

A Table, or a List with `edge="bleed"`, that is the first or last child of a rounded Card or Dialog that holds no other Table or bleeding List deeper inside now rounds with the corner it reaches, so the table's focus ring stays whole at the container's corners instead of being cut off. A bleeding List with a header rounds only its last row. Every other corner stays square: standalone, inside a square container or a wrapper element, between other content, at the top of a BottomSheet (below its grab bar), or while another Table or bleeding List sits deeper in the same container.

CodeBlock's "Failed to copy value to clipboard." announcement now uses the assertive live region instead of the polite one, as status announcements require for errors, so screen readers report a failed copy right away. A successful copy is still announced politely.

Internal: Core's internal touch entry re-exports the action-group tracking hook, which gains a no-paint option and press callbacks for Lab's TabBar. A tab-bar string joins Core's message catalog. Apps import nothing new.

Internal: the undocumented `@astryxdesign/core/internal/reorder` entry also gives Lab's `ListInput` List's reorder session for rows that are not ListItems: `useListReorderScope` and `ListReorderScope`. `List` runs its own rows' session through the same session hooks, so its callers see no change. A ListInput string joins Core's message catalog. Internal entries are outside the public API and its compatibility promise.

Internal: the undocumented `@astryxdesign/core/internal/reorder` entry lets Lab's `TransferList` and `TransferListSelector` reorder through a `createReorderable` object: `adaptReorderable` runs the owner's engine with the collection's own moves, and the owner's `start(key)` still finds the collection's list. Existing `List` callers are unchanged. Internal entries are outside the public API and its compatibility promise.
Internal: Core's internal touch entry re-exports its scroll test for Lab's TabBar. Apps import nothing new.

A swizzled `Outline` (or another copy that carries Core's Markdown plugin protocol) now type-checks against the package's Markdown plugins: `MarkdownPluginEntry` and `MarkdownTransform` carry their node type on a shared, versioned key instead of a module-local symbol, so the package's and the copy's types match. The member exists only in types; runtime trust and claim checks are unchanged. No API changes.

A swizzled copy and the package now agree on the animated-layout handle, code-language values and snap paging. A handle from `useAnimatedLayout` passed to a swizzled `AppShell`, `List`, `Table`, `TreeList`, `Collapsible` or `SideNav` no longer throws when the layout changes, and those copies type-check: each brand is read through a registered, versioned key at runtime, and the types carry one optional brand member that is never present. No API changes.

Core registers every React context, and the English its components register, under a versioned key, so two copies of Core's modules on one page share them: a provider from one copy reaches consumers from the other, a layer boundary from either resets the layer-scoped contexts of both, and a component from either shows its English. A copy built against another version of a context keeps its own. No API changes.

A swizzled component that carries Core's touch code, such as a swizzled `Switch` or `Slider`, now joins the package's gesture host, window input listeners, click guard, layer input holds and moving-element hit testing for the page instead of keeping a second set, so the copy and package components do not both claim the same touches. No API changes.

A swizzled `List`, `TransferList` or `ListInput` and the package now agree on a `createReorderable` object: its reorder machinery is read through a registered, versioned key. Before, a swizzled `List` found no machinery on an object from the package and showed no reorder handles. No API changes.

Internal: per-instance warning deduplication and temporary focus targets each have one shared owner in Core. Resizable, Dialog and TabList dedupe their development warnings through it, and Chat's Done button parks focus through it. Warning text and focus behavior are unchanged; apps import nothing new.
Internal: the More tab's label, a tab-bar string, joins Core's message catalog for Lab's TabBar. Apps import nothing new.

A new `Course Detail` page template: a long-form sales page for a single offering in two columns — the long read (a preview poster with a fact row, an about block with skill chips, a module syllabus whose sections collapse module by module, an instructor card, reviews with a scored-aspects panel, and a FAQ) beside a sticky enroll rail (the price with a compare-at, a self-paced or cohort start picker, and a weekly-pace slider that computes a finish date). Copy it with `astryx template course-detail <path>`.

A `DateInput` or `DateTimeInput` with `presentation="bottom-sheet"` no longer causes a hydration mismatch when the server and the browser are on different dates. The closed sheet's calendar now renders right after hydration, once the browser's today is known.

Dialog: under React StrictMode, a `Dialog` with a `DialogHeader` that is first mounted open and then removed while open (rendered only while open) now returns focus to the element that opened it, instead of leaving focus on the page body. The opener is captured only on the closed-to-open edge.

`Dialog`: a `DialogHeader` title now takes focus only after the dialog is modal, also when the header mounts in the render that opens the dialog. When no other control asks for focus, initial focus now starts on the title in every browser. Before, a header with a start control, and any header in Firefox, started on the first control.

A long-running process that calls the CLI's API, such as a docs site's search route, now reads an edited CommonJS `.doc.js` file again in docs, search and template reads. It read the doc as first loaded.

`astryx docs` also opens a docs-tree node by its bare name, or by a route that drops the prefix its name repeats, when exactly one node matches: `astryx docs tokens-color` and `astryx docs tokens/color` both open `tokens/tokens-color`. Two or more nodes answering one name still fail with the suggestions they always listed, and an experimental doc still opens only by its marked route.

`astryx docs --depth <levels>` now names the docs below each namespace on the topic list, by the route that opens them, so one read learns every route instead of one read per namespace. Without `--depth` the list is unchanged, and the JSON keeps its shape: the new `children` sit inside each `meta.namespaces` entry.

`Drawer`: a non-modal drawer (`hasScrim={false}`) that unmounts while it is open, for example one rendered only while open (`{isEditing && <Drawer isOpen …>}`) or removed with the rest of a view, now returns focus to the control that opened it instead of dropping it to the page. A modal drawer already did.

DropdownMenu: a finger's hold-slide-lift no longer flashes the focus outline on the menu button. When a held press opens the menu, the button takes focus first, so focus can return to it when the menu closes; that focus now shows the outline only after keyboard input. A keyboard open and close still show the outline on the button.

The File Explorer page template scrolls its columns with `StackItem` and `HStack` `isScrollable` instead of custom overflow and flex styles, and names each column after the folder it lists while the column scrolls. Its chevrons now mirror in right-to-left, and a detail pane scrolled to its end keeps its bottom padding.

Dialog, CommandPalette, BottomSheet, Lightbox, Drawer, MobileNav, Popover: Tab no longer escapes a modal through a radio group. The browser gives a same-name group of native radios one Tab stop: its checked radio, or, when none is checked, its first moving forward and its last moving backward. The focus region now finds its first and last stops the same way. Before, Tab from a group's checked radio left the modal for the browser's toolbar when the group ended the modal and that radio was not last in it, and Shift+Tab did the same when a group started it. Reported by @duytbp.

A command that reads a project module again after changing it, such as `astryx integration add` checking the manifest it just wrote, now reads the change for an ES module `.js` file in a package without a `"type"` field. It read the module as first loaded.

Gestures: a finger's lift is read on the clock its moves came on. In WebKit on Linux, a page pointerup listener that runs long no longer makes a fast flick read as a resting finger, or a tap lifted in time read as a long press.

Gothic: accent text and accent icons stay readable on a light media surface. They used Gothic's light accent there, near-white on a light band (1.14:1); now they follow the surface's dark accent (18.7:1 against a white surface). The CLI's Gothic theme template carries the same change.

Hook docs for `useCalendarConstraints`, so `astryx hook useCalendarConstraints` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useCalendarConstraints — Hotel Booking Range` example block: a booking range picker that enforces min/max dates, disables closed Mondays, and caps reservations at 7 nights once check-in is selected. Copy it with `astryx template useCalendarConstraintsHookUsage <path>`.

Hook docs for `useCalendarNavigation`, so `astryx hook useCalendarNavigation` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useCalendarNavigation — Month Pager` example block: a month-by-month calendar with Previous/Next controls, localized month-year header, and cross-month arrow key navigation using `pendingFocus`. Copy it with `astryx template useCalendarNavigationHookUsage <path>`.

Hook docs for `useLinkify`, so `astryx hook useLinkify` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useLinkify — Links in a Comment Thread` example block: plain-text comments where the URL and email become Links and a custom `#123` issue-reference pattern shows the patterns option, while a comment without matches stays plain.
Add usePowerSearchConfig hook docs and a filtered directory table example block
Add useTableColumnSettingsState hook docs and a column visibility picker example block

A `useInteractiveRole — One Tile, Four Roles` example block for the existing hook docs: a polymorphic Tile rendered four ways — href link, onClick button, Popover-trigger context button, inert content — showing the resolution order in one place.

Fix the `useStreamingText — Streaming Response` example block: it passed `isStreaming` as `false`, so the streaming reveal it exists to show never ran. The block is now a chat-style reply card with a Regenerate button that streams the response in bursts — the hook reveals it steadily while streaming and snaps to the full text when it ends.

`HoverCard` and `useHoverCard` no longer open on keyboard focus of the trigger while `isOpen={false}` is passed. The controlled `false` already refused hover, but tabbing onto the trigger opened the card and reported `onOpenChange(true)` against the owner's state; focus now takes the same refusal as hover.

HoverCard: a trigger inside SVG `<foreignObject>` cannot be a CSS anchor in Chromium, so its card opens at the viewport corner. The docs now say so and show the fix: render the trigger in an HTML layer positioned over the SVG node.

HoverCard: a labelled card no longer puts `aria-haspopup="dialog"` on a role-less trigger, such as text or a `<time>`. Such a trigger names the open card through `aria-controls` only; a button or link trigger still gets `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`.

A `HoverCard` rendered into another document, such as an iframe or a Picture-in-Picture window, now closes when Escape is pressed there, and Escape from inside the card returns focus to its trigger. Moving focus from the trigger into such a card also keeps it open. Before, the card read only the page's document, so Escape in the other document never closed it. The card now also ranks on the shared dismissal stack by its trigger's place, so a card whose trigger sits inside a focus-trap container takes Escape before that container, as the topmost layer.

`HoverCard` and `Tooltip`: a controlled `isOpen={true}` (or `isDefaultOpen`) no longer strands the layer in the viewport corner when its trigger mounts with no layout box yet, for example inside a `Dialog` that has not called `showModal()` yet.
changesets.body:
`Dialog` mounts its children before it opens (`isOpen` gates `showModal()`, not rendering), so a `HoverCard` or `Tooltip` inside one with a controlled `isOpen={true}` runs its show effect while the trigger sits in a still non-modal `<dialog>` and has no box. A trigger with no box is not a valid CSS anchor: the popover resolves to its fallback position in the viewport corner, and unlike a live layout change that resolution is not revisited once the trigger later gets a box.

`Layer`'s `show()` now opens immediately when the trigger already has a layout box (an empty one, such as a ContextMenu's cursor anchor, counts), so a menu or popover still opens in the same task as the press that asked for it. Only a trigger with no layout box (`display: none`, or inside a `<dialog>` that is not showing) waits: first for it to get a layout box and for its dialog to show, then for any running animation on the document timeline that ends on its own, on the trigger or an ancestor, to finish, so the layer anchors to the trigger's settled position and not to a mid-transition one. Paused, infinite, and scroll- or view-driven animations are not waited on.

The box wait is driven by signals and polls nothing: a `ResizeObserver` for a trigger that gains a layout box, an `IntersectionObserver` for a purely `display: inline` trigger (such as the wrapper `<span>` of a text-only trigger), which a `ResizeObserver` never delivers an entry for, and the enclosing dialog's `open` attribute and `toggle` event. A dialog counts as showing when it is open or shown as a popover, so triggers inside a non-modal `Drawer` still open their layers. The wait has no time limit and ends when the trigger gets a box inside a showing dialog or the open is cancelled (a later `show()` or `hide()`, or unmount). If the trigger element is replaced while waiting, the wait restarts on the new one, and a trigger that unmounts for good stops observing. Without a layout engine to wait on (no `ResizeObserver` or no Web Animations API, as in jsdom) the layer opens immediately.

A transient `null` then same-element call on the trigger ref, as a combined ref utility makes when a handler changes identity, no longer removes and re-adds the element's `anchor-name`, which could also leave an open layer stranded in the corner.

changesets.headline: Icon sets: an icon whose name would start with a digit once the library prefix comes off, such as a library's `fa0`, now keeps that prefix: it gets id `fa-0` and is exported as `Fa0Icon` (`fa500px` becomes `Fa500pxIcon`). The CLI wrote `0Icon` before, which is not a valid JavaScript name, so the generated module did not parse. An id you give that starts with a digit, with no prefix to keep, is refused with a message that asks for an id that starts with a letter. Only `experimental icon new-set --from` and `experimental icon add` change; a set they write now passes `integration check`.

Icon sets: `integration check` now accepts a generated declaration file (`*.generated.d.ts`) whose long type arguments a formatter such as Prettier re-wrapped. Before, the re-wrapped line made the check report `icon_generated_types_mismatch` and fail. A changed declaration still fails the check. The experimental icon commands are unchanged.

Icon sets: `experimental icon add --variant <look> --from <module> --all` now works for a library that ships each look as its own package, such as Font Awesome's solid and regular packages of icon data objects. Before, it found no icon to give the variant, because every icon came from another package. An icon gains the variant from the export of the same name and kind, and the receipt lists as missing the icons of that library that the look's package does not export. Wrapping such a library also no longer turns a pack export (`fas`, an object of the other exports) into an icon, so the shared `fa` prefix comes off the names again. A name that would then start with a digit keeps the prefix (`fa0` becomes `Fa0Icon`), so the generated module still parses. Only the experimental icon commands and `integration check` on an icon set change.

Icon sets: after you rename an icon-set package in package.json, the next `experimental icon` command that writes the data file (`new-set` on the existing set, with or without `--from`, `add`, `map`, or `new-definition --icon`, even one that changes nothing else) writes the new package name to the data file's `module`, and keeps any subpath (`@acme/old-icons/outline` becomes `@acme/new-icons/outline`). Before, the old name stayed, and `integration check` failed until you edited the file by hand. The receipt of each of these commands names the new and the old `module` (`Updated module to "@acme/new-icons/outline" (was "@acme/old-icons/outline"), from the package name in package.json.`), and `map` words each `map` entry from what it replaced, so an entry that did not change says so. Only the experimental icon commands and the icon-sets guide change.

Layers with an entrance input hold: a finger or pen that was already down when a light-dismissing layer opened, and lifts while it enters, now lifts through the hold's shield onto what is under it in WebKit, so the layer dismisses as it already did in Chromium. The shield leaves a small opening at each such press until it lifts. New presses during the entrance are still held.
Internal: Core's internal finger-scroll reader can answer for a past time on the page's clock, for Lab's NavigationStack scroll edge. Apps import nothing new.
`Kbd` shows `meta` as ⌘ on Apple platforms, where it showed "META".

`Kbd` shows `ctrl`, `alt` and `shift` as text ("Ctrl", "Alt", "Shift") off Apple platforms and before hydration, and `meta` as "Win" off Apple platforms and before hydration, instead of Apple's ⌃ ⌥ ⇧ symbols and "META". Apple platforms keep the symbols, and spoken names are unchanged. The text comes from the catalog, so other locales can translate it.

Closing a Popover or DropdownMenu with Escape, or a DropdownMenu with a pick or a press on its trigger, runs one layout again, not two. A closed trigger stops being a CSS anchor, and these closes took the trigger's anchor name away after the hide's own layout, so the browser laid out once more. Our hide now drops the name before its layout, unless the layer's closed state keeps it shown to fade out. A close the browser runs itself, such as a light dismiss, still drops the name at its toggle event. A layer that fades out keeps the name until its fade ends.

Layer: a light-dismissible layer that opens from a right click's `contextmenu` event stays open when that same press is released. Before, the release counted as a press outside, so a DropdownMenu opened through `isMenuOpen` from a right click closed at once. A later press outside still dismisses the layer.

Popover, DropdownMenu and its submenus, Selector, ComplexSelector, PowerSearch and Breadcrumbs' menu play their entrance on the surface inside the layer, not on the anchored layer. Chromium laid the anchored layer out again on every frame of its 150 ms entrance, two to four times per frame, whenever the page had other frame work. The entrance looks the same. `layerAnimations` is unchanged; its docs now say to apply it to the surface. Applied to the layer, it still plays as before.

A popover taller than the room on both sides of its trigger keeps its top when the keyboard shortens it. The field being typed into stays under the caret. It used to jump below the trigger as the keyboard arrived, and back as it went.

Once the keyboard caps a layer such as a popover, a scroll a person starts in it afterwards is no longer undone. On a busy page, the layer could scroll back to the focused field just after. A later keyboard change still brings the field being typed into back into view.

A Tooltip, including a Slider's value bubble, no longer jumps to another side of its trigger in the middle of a scroll. Before, when a scroll carried the trigger toward the edge, the layer runtime took the Tooltip out of rendering for one forced layout so the browser would choose its position again, and it did this again on later frames of the scroll. Now the Tooltip has one fallback list from the start, and no option in it covers the trigger: it tries the opposite side first, then beside the trigger, then a side sized to the room. During a scroll, the Tooltip keeps its side: it is not checked or placed afresh until the scroll stops. In the first frame painted after the scroll stops (at `scrollend`, or 150 ms after the last `scroll` event where the browser has no `scrollend`), it is checked once and moves to the side with room if it needs to. At a show, a remount or a size change it is checked as before.

A Tooltip's content scrolls by CSS alone, and nothing watches its trigger move. A Tooltip now has `overflow-y: auto` from its first frame, with no overscroll containment. It scrolls only while its content overflows, so a wheel over a Tooltip that fits still scrolls the page. Once a tall Tooltip has scrolled to its end, the next wheel moves on to the page, where before the page held. A Tooltip is now always a scroll container, so `position: sticky` and `scroll(nearest)` timelines inside its content resolve against the Tooltip. The layer runtime no longer reads the Tooltip's scroll size after its trigger moves, and it no longer observes a trigger that moves without resizing.

While a Tooltip or another anchored layer plays its entrance, most reads of the layer's box write no styles. Before, each read during the entrance overrode the layer's transform, read the box and put the transform back, so the browser recomputed style and layout twice in that frame (measured in Chromium: 8 style writes, 2 style recalculations and 2 layouts per read). Now a read on the middle frames of an entrance takes the entrance transform out of one box read by calculation, and gets the same box. The read that shows the layer and any read while its entrance is pending, a read whose box does not yet carry the entrance (in Chromium, a layer at a fallback position), the last frames of an entrance, a layer under a CSS `zoom` other than 1, and a `translate` given as a percentage still use the override, as before. Placement, the entrance animation and the keyboard cap do not change.

A swizzled `LayerProvider` now shows the package's toasts: the viewport the package's `Toast` registers renders in a copied provider's outlet, and the package's provider renders a copy's. Before, each copy kept its own registry, so toasts added under a swizzled provider never showed. The registry lives under a registered, versioned key. No API changes.

`Layout`: a `false`, `true`, or empty-string slot, such as `false` from `isOpen && <LayoutPanel />`, now counts as empty. The neighbouring regions move out to the layout edge, the same as when the slot is omitted, and with `contentWidth` a closed side panel no longer stops the content area at the content-width frame. The docs now list `children` and `ref`, show how to hide a region, and say that landmark roles go on the region components.

`LayoutContent`: the edge away from a single start panel now takes the Layout-edge inset, so `padding={0}` on the Layout makes it full bleed, and with `contentWidth` its children end one Layout-edge inset inside the content-width frame, as they do without panels. Each edge now publishes the padding it applies, so a full-bleed child such as a Table lines up beside an end panel and under a header without a divider. A Layout nested under a header or footer without a divider keeps its own content spacing instead of taking the outer collapse.

A `Layout` with no `contentWidth` no longer caps its `LayoutHeader` and `LayoutFooter` at the viewport's width. In a frame wider than the viewport, such as a scrolling canvas or a wide embed, their content now spans the frame like the rest of the Layout.

`LayoutFooter`: a `data-divider` attribute passed by the caller no longer replaces the divider state the footer reflects, so the content above a footer without a divider keeps its collapsed spacing, and a footer with a divider keeps its spacing above the line. The docs now list `padding` and `ref`, and say that an unset `hasDivider` follows the Layout's `defaultHasDividers`.

`LayoutHeader`: a `data-divider` attribute passed by the caller no longer replaces the divider state the header reflects, so the content below a header without a divider keeps its collapsed spacing, and a header with a divider keeps its spacing below the line. The docs now list `padding` and `ref`, and say that an unset `hasDivider` follows the Layout's `defaultHasDividers`.

`LayoutPanel`: on an edge that takes the Layout's own inset, the panel now tells its children the padding it applies there. Children that read their container's padding, such as a full-bleed `Divider`, `Table`, or `TabList`, or a nested `Layout`, now follow the panel's outer edge whenever the Layout's `padding` differs from the inner inset. Before, they used the inner inset: with `padding={6}` a full-bleed `Divider` stopped 8px short of the edge, and with `padding={0}` it ran 16px past it. The docs now say which edge `hasDivider` draws on, that the Layout's `defaultHasDividers` does not apply, and that `padding={0}` is full bleed, and they list `ref`.

A `LayoutPanel` that takes a `useResizable` region in its `resizable` prop slides closed and open from the edge facing its `ResizeHandle` when the region collapses or opens, under every pointer, with the content beside it moving on the same motion: through `collapse()`, `expand()`, Enter, a double-click, the grow arrow, a controlled `isCollapsed`, or a lift past the collapse threshold. A drag that reopens the panel follows the pointer, and Reduce Motion is honored. A hand-built `ResizableProps` object does not slide. No prop or option is added.
`LayoutPanel`'s JSDoc example wraps its Layout in a `Card` instead of `LayoutContainer`, a component Astryx does not have.

`Lightbox`: a screen reader now hears the viewer's own messages while it is open. Moving to another item ("Mountain lake, 2 of 4") and zooming in or out are announced inside the open viewer; before, they went to the page behind the modal viewer, where a screen reader does not read them. The `0` key now returns a zoomed photo to its fitted size. The docs list the `0` key, and no longer say that the lightbox is only for images.
Lightbox's drag to close now plays at the theme's tempo, like the viewer's other motion. At the default tempo it plays exactly as before.

On a phone or tablet, drag a Lightbox photo down to close the viewer, as in the iOS Photos viewer. The photo follows your finger and shrinks a little as you pull, while the backdrop fades and the controls fade faster. The backdrop fades without its blur, which comes back once it is at rest. Let go moving down, however short the pull, and the photo carries on down as the viewer closes. Flick it back up, or bring it back to where you started, and it springs back into place. A zoomed photo still pans when you drag it; the drag to close starts from the fitted size. Videos are unchanged.
changesets.body: The viewer's controls now sit in their own layers, which fade together during the drag.

changesets.headline: A Lightbox gallery now pages the way the iOS Photos viewer does. On a phone or tablet, drag or flick between items: the row follows your finger, and the release lands on the next or previous item, one at most. A gap of 40 px separates the items while they move. A zoomed photo pans with your finger until it reaches its edge; a new drag from that edge moves to the next item. A photo you leave zoomed returns to its fitted size once the gallery rests. Under a finger, the previous and next buttons and the arrow keys slide to the item instead of swapping it in place.
changesets.body:
Each item's caption moves with its item, right under its photo. `onIndexChange` also reports a swipe.

Lightbox now loads its touch code with it, as Toast and Slider do. Its import grows from 51.4 KB to 99.6 KB gzip with the zoom and paging beneath, mostly shared touch modules that a page loads once; Lightbox's own code adds 14.1 KB minified.

changesets.headline: An open Lightbox shows the nearest item when `index` or `defaultIndex` is NaN or a fraction between the first and last item. A fraction rounds to the nearest item, and NaN shows the first item. Before, the viewer rendered nothing for those values.

Internal: the undocumented `@astryxdesign/core/internal/line-clamp` entry gives Lab's `LineClamp` Core's focusable selector, the shared mutation observer and its flush, and the shared truncation tooltip. The shared mutation observer now passes each registration the records that reached it, and existing callers ignore them, so their behaviour is unchanged. Internal entries are outside the public API and its compatibility promise.
The official-packages discovery list now includes the Lab `LineClamp` component, so `astryx` can find and describe it.

`List` takes `animatedLayout`, the handle from `useAnimatedLayout({containerRef})`, and `ListItem` takes `itemKey`, the row's identity. With the handle, when rows are inserted, removed or reordered, an inserted row enters, a removed row (a swiped one with its action showing) collapses in place, and a row that crosses rows moving the other way rides above them with the surface color behind it, as an iOS table's opaque cell does. The rows after a change and the content after the list, up to the handle's container, glide to their new places. All of it runs on one shared motion and starts together, under every pointer; under Reduce Motion nothing travels. A row without an `itemKey` changes at once, and without the handle the whole list does.

While a reorderable `List` row is in reorder mode, a hint anchored to its handle, in the keyboard hint's layer and theme roles, shows the moves and Done. Each is a button that does what its key does and leaves the focus on the handle, so a row can be reordered by taps alone: the handle, the moves, then Done.

A reorderable `List` in its own scroll box keeps the dragged row under the pointer when a wheel during a mouse or pen drag scrolls the page, as a wheel at the box's end does. The wheel scrolls as before.

`createReorderable({onReorder, isReorderable})` makes a collection's reorder behavior, and `List` takes it as `reorderable`: each `ListItem` with an `itemKey` gets a reorder handle at its end, and each committed move calls `onReorder({key, to})` once, with the row's key and its index after the move. On a touch screen a finger held still on a handle picks up its row the way an iOS table's reorder control does (a flick on it still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near the edges, and on release the rows rearrange, gliding to their new places. A pen held on a handle picks up its row the same way where the primary pointer is coarse. A mouse, or a pen where the primary pointer is fine, drags a handle at once with the same copy and line, and rows take their places without motion; a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. Without a drag, a click, Space or Enter on a handle turns on reorder mode for its row: the insertion line marks the row's place, each arrow key moves it a place at once, announced with its place and neighbours, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves. The object's `start(key)` enters the same mode from the app's own UI, such as a row's context menu. A List without `reorderable` loads none of the reorder code.

Markdown: each paragraph, heading, quote and list item lays out in the direction of its own text. A Hebrew or Arabic paragraph in a left-to-right page now starts on the right, and an English paragraph in a right-to-left page starts on the left. A block with no letters, such as digits, punctuation or an image, takes the page's direction from the `InternationalizationProvider`, also inside a quote or list item that reads the other way. Lists, code blocks and tables keep the direction around them too, and the text in each table cell reads in its own direction. A numbered item that reads against its list shows its number beside its own text, and a table cell that reads against its table keeps the table's column lines and any explicit column alignment. A task list now keeps to the same prose width as other lists.

Menus: the arrow keys, Home, End and type-ahead now reach a disabled row in `DropdownMenu`, its sub-menus, `MoreMenu`, `ContextMenu` and `NavHeadingMenu`, so a keyboard or screen-reader user finds the row and its description. The row takes focus, is announced as disabled, and Enter, Space or a click on it still does nothing and leaves the menu open. Opening a menu from the keyboard still lands on an enabled row.

DropdownMenu: a held mouse dragged from the trigger onto a row keeps that row lit. On a loaded page the menu's open focus could land after the drag reached the row and take the highlight back to the menu container until the pointer moved again.

DropdownMenu: a menu that a mouse press opens stays open when that press is released quickly away from the trigger, or after the trigger moved away under the pointer. Before, the browser's light dismiss read that release as a press outside and closed the menu at once. A press released after the settle time outside the menu still closes it, and a later press outside dismisses it.
Under a finger, the month and year wheels behind the calendar title in the DateInput and DateTimeInput bottom sheets now behave like the iOS date picker's:
changesets.body:
- Turning a wheel moves a chosen date to the new month and keeps its day, so October 15 becomes May 15. A day the month lacks becomes its last day, the result stays within `min` and `max`, and DateTimeInput keeps the time. A date that `dateConstraints` refuses is not chosen; the calendar still moves.
- With no date chosen, the wheels only move the calendar.

With a mouse, the wheels still move only the calendar.

changesets.headline: Motion: a Switch at rest holds no compositing layer under a coarse pointer. Its colour fade and its lift's shadow take a layer only while they move.

Motion: elements that start moving from rest in the same frame now start at one time. Before, each element took its own reading of the clock in that frame, so items starting together, such as a carousel's pages as they settle, could start apart by as long as the frame callbacks between them ran.

Motion: the motions that one callback starts on elements that came in the same task read their stylesheets' `will-change` in one style pass, after the callback. Before, each element forced a style pass of its own: eight for a list whose eight rows glide together.

Motion: a spring retarget that the browser commits late, behind a busy main thread, now starts at that frame, from where the element is on screen. Before, it kept the clock of the call, so the element jumped to where the new curve had got to: 42 px back in one frame for a retarget behind a 200 ms block. Motion calls made in one callback now share one clock, so the children of a pager line up after a retarget. A retarget made inside a page's own frame or ResizeObserver callback now shows its new curve one frame later.

MultiSelector: opening the closed list never highlights a disabled option. ArrowDown, Enter, Space and a press highlight the first enabled option in the order the list opens in, and ArrowUp the last, so Enter no longer lands on an option it cannot toggle. A list with search still highlights nothing when a press or Enter opens it.

Neutral: an unselected SegmentedControl label meets 4.5:1 in dark mode on AppShell's surface. The track is translucent, so it lightens the surface under the label: `#9e9e9e` on `#3c3c3c` measured 4.11:1. The label now takes `neutral.dark[80]` (6.46:1), the same lift Neutral already gives secondary text on its selected rows and pills. Light mode is unchanged, and the CLI's Neutral theme template matches.

ChatLayout's guidance explains how a reply gets one right edge: Markdown prose keeps its 680px measure while code blocks and tables span the message column, so pass `contentWidth="100%"` to the reply's Markdown. Markdown's default measure is unchanged. (#5598)

Internal: the layer's outside-press watch can follow chosen pointer types, close as a press that starts outside begins to pan (on either axis, at core's pan threshold) or when the browser takes it, and judge a press inside a closed shadow root, which the document sees as its host. No component passes these options yet, so every watch keeps today's behavior. Not exported from the package entry point.
Carousel paging: a finger or a pen that lands on a row still settling after a swipe no longer reaches the item under it: no press highlight and no click, as on iOS. A mouse click is unchanged.

Carousel paging: a finger or a pen that lands on the row during an edge button's move now stops it at the touch, as on iOS, instead of letting it run on for about 85 ms. The item under the finger still takes the tap. A mouse is unchanged.

A page that a swipe releases now settles at the theme's `tempo`, as the rest of its motion does: in a `Carousel` given `hasSnap={useSnapPaging()}`, and in a `Lightbox` gallery. At the default tempo the settle is unchanged.

`Pagination`'s ellipsis grows with a larger text size, as its page buttons now do through `Button`. Its size is now a minimum height, so the "…" stays inside its own box. At the default text size nothing changes.

`Pagination` wraps its row when its controls don't fit, as at a larger text size on a phone, instead of scrolling the page sideways and pushing Next off-screen. Previous stays first and Next stays last. Beside other content in a flex row, Pagination can now shrink to its widest control and wrap at the default text size too, where it held one line before; give it `flexShrink: 0` through `xstyle` to keep one line there.

`parseColor` answers `null` for `constructor` and `__proto__` (in any case), as for any unknown name, instead of a truthy empty RGBA that made composed callers such as chart `colors.alpha` return `rgba(NaN, NaN, NaN, …)` (or `#NANNANNAN` at full opacity) instead of the original string (#10468)

A closed `Popover`, and any `usePopover` composition, no longer leaves a hidden `role="dialog"` with its label in the DOM. The surface stays mounted but carries the dialog role, name and `aria-modal` only while open, so `[role="dialog"]` selectors and tests that include hidden elements find no dialog that is not on screen. The accessibility tree already omitted the hidden surface. Reopening restores them.

A dialog Popover starts focus on its first enabled tab stop. It skips a disabled control, lets an element that holds `tabindex="-1"` yield to a later tab stop, and starts on its labelled surface when every control is disabled. Before, a DateInput or DateTimeInput calendar whose range starts in the shown month opened on the disabled Previous month button. Now it opens on Next month, or, in a one-month range, on the selected day, else today, else the first enabled day. Disabled controls stay reachable by Tab.

Under a finger, Popover's growth shows its content from its first frame. The growth starts at opacity 0.001 rather than 0: Chromium skips drawing a layer at exactly 0, so the first frames of a growth from 0 showed the popover without its content. No 8-bit pixel differs from transparent at 0.001.

Internal: Popover keeps its chosen presentation (the sheet or the anchored layer, the touch grow or the pointer entrance) from the open until its close settles through the layer runtime's one presentation hold (Layer/presentationHold.ts). No behavior change.

Under a finger, Popover plays its growth on the surface inside the layer, not on the anchored layer. Chromium restyles the growth's animations twice as they start and once as they end, and each restyle laid the anchored layer out twice, its backdrop included. Under load those layouts landed inside the growth. The popover looks the same.
In PowerSearch's phone sheet, a date range is now picked on a calendar inside the sheet, instead of a calendar popover opening over it. The desktop editor popover is unchanged.

PowerSearch's phone sheet now edits single and multiple choices with the standard RadioList and CheckboxList at their usual spacing, instead of its own 48 px rows, and its Operator radios put the radio at the start of the row, as every RadioList does. The choices use the shared touch band, so their touch targets are smaller than before. End, Home and Enter no longer pick a choice; the arrow keys and Space work as in any RadioList or CheckboxList. Adds a "Sheet presentation · realistic config" story that covers every value type. The desktop editor popover is unchanged.

`PowerSearch`: a filter token's field and operator now come from one catalog message (`@astryx.powersearch.token.fieldOperator`, "{field}: {operator}" in English), and its full text, which also names its remove button and editor, joins that label and the value with another (`@astryx.powersearch.token.labelValue`, "{label} {value}"). A locale can reorder the parts and change the punctuation. `PowerSearchToken` uses the same message. English tokens read as before, except that a filter with no operator text no longer shows a trailing colon.

Press feedback: a `pointerup` that carries no `pointerId`, such as a bare event a test helper or drag script dispatches, no longer throws `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'live')` when no press is held. It is ignored, as `pointercancel` already does.

Inside a scroll view, a pressable's highlight now comes 150 ms after the touch, even when a busy page handles the touch late. Before, the wait started when the page handled the touch, so the highlight came late by that delay. This covers every pressable, and SegmentedControl, Switch, Slider and `usePressTracker` controls, in a scroll view.
A theme duration token written with `calc()` now times a press's release as the browser resolves it. Before, the release clock fell back to 175 ms while the fade played the token's value.

useClickableContainer documents a pressable surface without Card chrome: the hook on the surface, `usePressFeedback` with `interactionOverlayStyles.backgroundColor` for the hover tint and touch press, a visually hidden `<button>` or `<a>` as the named control, and `focusOutlineStyles.focusWithin` for the shared focus ring that ClickableCard draws. ClickableCard's docs point chrome-free use to it.

`astryx build`: when an idea names a family only after its head ("a saml for a login") and the family's base template matches no other word, the variant that outranks the base now stays the start (`login-sso`, not `login`), so adding page templates no longer flips such ideas to the base. Ideas that name the family in their head ("saml login") start as before.

`astryx experimental render` draws recharts charts. A recharts chart draws only after its effects run, and a `ResponsiveContainer` measures its parent in a browser, so a rendered page showed an empty box for every chart. The render now draws each chart and `ResponsiveContainer` a page imports from recharts by name, after the server render, in a small document with no layout. A container starts at its own width and height, or at a width that follows its height, and the drawing scales to the width the page gives it. The `chart-size` warning counts the charts the render could not draw, and says when charts were drawn by themselves (when the page cannot be drawn again without a browser, or its effects change its charts or re-render the component that makes them). Charts show the data and props of the page's first render; a value a chart's parts read from a React context that an effect changes may show its later value.

[experimental] `astryx experimental render` no longer dies silently with exit 139 when Node itself crashes while it renders a page. The page now renders in a separate process, so a crash (a crash signal, or a crash status on Windows) ends only that process, and the render fails with `ERR_RENDER_FAILED` and a message that names the Node version and path; a signal that stops it names them too. That process ends when the CLI ends, so a page that never finishes does not outlive a stopped CLI. Some Node builds crash in `Intl.Segmenter`, which components such as Avatar use to split text: on such a build the render runs the page once more without `Intl.Segmenter` and adds a `node-crash` warning that names the Node build and says the output may differ slightly (a joined emoji, a flag, or a letter with a separate accent mark in initials), so pages with Avatar render again.

The `collapsible`, `collapsedSize`, `isCollapsed` and `onCollapseChange` descriptions in the Resizable and `useResizable` docs name what collapses a region, a lift or a key step under the collapsed size rather than a drag alone, and what reports a collapse change.

A `ResizeHandle` that any pointer pulls past the maximum, or under the minimum, of a region whose pane a `LayoutPanel` renders now moves the handle with resistance, at most about 8 px past the limit and over the content beside it, while the panes keep their sizes, and the handle springs back to the limit after the lift. A panel sized by the region's `size` alone stops at the limit. A collapsible region no longer collapses mid-drag: only the lift collapses it, when the pointer is past `collapsedSize`, or released fast enough to come to rest past it, and a `LayoutPanel`'s pane slides shut on a spring from the release velocity. Any other lift under the minimum returns to the minimum. A pointer that grabs the handle again catches it where it shows. Arrow keys still stop at the limit. Reduce Motion lands both at once.

`RichTextEditorAutoLinkPlugin` no longer turns a URL inside a code block into a link. A URL typed or pasted into a code block, or one in an imported fence, now stays code. Before, the link nested inside the code block, and the exported Markdown fence lost it.

In `RichTextEditor`, pasting rich content into a code block inserts plain text: the plain text on the clipboard, or, when there is none, each pasted block as one line of its text. Headings, lists, tables, and formatting used to land inside the code block, where the Markdown export wrote them as plain lines of the fence, so the document read back differently from what the editor showed.

In `RichTextEditor`, Tab and Shift+Tab in a code block indent and outdent every line the selection touches, by the indent the block already uses (a tab when one of its lines starts with a tab, otherwise the fewest leading spaces of any indented line, kept between 2 and 8, otherwise 2 spaces). The selection stays on the same characters and each press is one undo step. Tab used to put a tab character in place of the selection, and Shift+Tab did the same. Escape then Tab still moves focus out of the editor.
`RichTextView`, `RichTextEditorToolbar` and `RichTextEditorAutoLinkPlugin` each ship a doc file, so `astryx component`, `astryx discover` and the docs list their props, defaults and usage.

A link inside a disabled `RichTextEditor` no longer navigates, shows no pointer cursor, and is not a tab stop. Before, a disabled editor's links acted as live links: a click or Enter opened them, and Tab stopped on each one.
A source comment in the editor theme now says that core `Markdown` gives each block the direction of its own text, while the editor keeps blocks in the surface's direction.

RichTextEditor documents how to switch between reading and editing in place without reflow: set the field's inset and border outside the reading width with `xstyle`, so every paragraph keeps its line count across the switch. A standalone editor keeps its form width.

Internal: one owner module now turns the browser's scroll anchoring off on a container whose position a component owns. `useChatStreamScroll` uses it while it follows the end, with the same behaviour as before, and the undocumented `@astryxdesign/core/internal/scroll-anchoring` entry gives its writer to Lab. Internal entries are outside the public API and its compatibility promise.

Two loads of Core's scroll-lock modules on one page now share one page scroll lock: closing the overlay that opened first no longer unlocks the page while the other overlay is still open. Text-selection locks, which a swizzled copy carries, are shared the same way, so a copy's release no longer restores a selection lock the package still holds. No API changes.

useScrollableArea: an ancestor's inline `style` change measures the scroll area again only when it changes the axis mapping or the boxes' existence (`direction`, `writing-mode`, `display`, `visibility`, `content-visibility`); a size change still reaches it through the resize observers. A BottomSheet writes its transform, and its scrim's custom property, on every input sample of a drag, and each write forced a full measurement (its computed-style reads and the scroll geometry) in the next frame, a style recalculation and a layout on every frame of the drag.
`getContentProps` from `useScrollableArea` now applies a caller's `xstyle` instead of leaking it to the DOM. (#6314)
changesets.body: A viewport that lost overflow while focused drops its leftover `tabindex` as soon as it is blurred, and a focused viewport in another document keeps focus when it loses overflow. `ScrollableArea`'s viewport also sheds the obsolete `-webkit-overflow-scrolling` and initial-value scrollbar declarations.

changesets.headline: `astryx search` puts the results that fit the whole query higher. The first result stays the same. At the default limit, and at any limit of 10 or more, the set of results stays the same. A smaller `--limit` shows the top of the new order, so it can show a different result. Below the first result, inside each group of equally strong matches, a result whose docs fit the query much worse than the others in its group moves after them. A result whose name spells two or more of the query's words never moves down; it can still move up. The fit uses the same word-meaning weights `astryx build` uses to pick blocks, so a new component or template is placed from its own docs. A query that is an entry's whole name keeps its answer.

`exportSearchIndex()` and `rankSearchIndex()` from `@astryxdesign/cli/api` store and rank search's candidates. `exportSearchIndex({cwd, package})` returns `{version, candidates}`: what `search()` ranks in a folder, as plain JSON (with `package`, only that package's entries). `rankSearchIndex(query, indexes, {type, limit})` ranks stored indexes with search's own tree: an index made in a project answers as `search(query)` does there, with the same response; for an index made outside a project, theme results name `theme add` where `search` there names `theme eject`. A catalog that lists packages it must not load makes the index where loading is safe and ranks it per query. An index is ranked only by the CLI version that made it. Both are experimental (they may change in a patch release), and their docs are not search results, so `search` and `build` answer exactly as before. When they are promoted to stable, their docs join search.
Section's docs show how to center it: set `marginInlineStart` and `marginInlineEnd` to `'auto'` in `xstyle`.

SegmentedControl: the label contrast guidance says the track is translucent, so label contrast depends on the background behind the control, and asks you to check the labels on every background it sits on, including a custom page color.

Selector: when the options move or reload while the list is open, the highlight stays on its option instead of naming whatever option now sits at its old position. If its option leaves, the highlight moves to the next remaining enabled option after it, or the previous one when none remains after it, and with none left nothing is highlighted.

`Selector` and `useCombobox`: opening a closed list starts on the selected option, as the WAI-ARIA listbox pattern asks, and never on a disabled option. Before, ArrowDown and ArrowUp opened on the first or last option even when it was disabled, and ArrowDown then Enter changed "Hard" to the first option. Now opening highlights the selected option when it is enabled. Otherwise ArrowUp opens on the last enabled option and ArrowDown, a press, Enter or Space on the first; with no enabled option nothing is highlighted. A search list opened by a press, Enter or typing still highlights nothing. `MultiSelector` is unchanged.

A Selector whose trigger sits near the bottom of the screen now opens its list on screen. The selected-item overlay's clamp did not count the layer's viewport gutter, so near the bottom edge the browser flipped the list below the viewport and its last options could not be reached.

Internal: Selector and MultiSelector keep the presentation an opening chose, and a closing sheet mounted until its focus handoff, through the layer runtime's presentation hold (Layer/presentationHold.ts). No behavior change.

In a searchable `Selector` or `MultiSelector`, typing now clears the highlight, so Enter never picks an option you did not highlight. Before, the highlight kept its old position, which could point at a different option of the filtered list or at nothing. ArrowDown then starts at the first row: the first enabled match in `Selector`, and Select all or the create row when shown in `MultiSelector`.

Selector with `hasSearch`: a required field no longer puts `aria-required` on its trigger, a button where the attribute is not allowed. The search field carries it while the list is open, and the closed trigger still announces "Required", through the field label or, when the label shows no marker, through its description.
Internal: Core's shared-realm module gains helpers for state that the package and a swizzled copy share (state, maps, stores, brands and sequences). No API or behavior changes.
SideNavCollapseButton's docs now list every key its `collapsible` prop takes: the whole controlled config SideNav gets, not only `isCollapsed` and `onCollapsedChange`.

`SideNav` no longer adds space below a `footer` when it has no `footerIcons` and no built-in collapse button. The sidebar rendered an empty footer row there, and the gap of the sticky bottom area added space after the footer. The row now renders only when it holds the collapse button or `footerIcons`, as the drawer already does.

Navigation rows grow with a larger text size. The shared nav item styles (`navItemStyles`, used by `SideNavItem` and by `TopNavItem` and the mega menu in the mobile drawer) now take their size as a minimum height instead of a fixed one, so above 200% text a row's label no longer overlaps the next row, and its end content (such as a count `Badge`) stays inside the row. Collapsed rail rows keep their fixed square. At the default text size, TopNav drawer menu and mega menu rows with a description now fit their text instead of overlapping the next row; other rows are unchanged. A caller `height` on these styles no longer brings a row below its size; override `minHeight` instead.
The `Skeleton` `radius` prop's description no longer says `4` is 16px. `4` maps to the same container radius as `3` (12px), so the two values draw the same corners. No behavior change.

Carousel snap paging: a stop that sits within half a step of the row's end is part of the last page, so a flick, a wheel or a key never rests a pixel short of the end, and a step back from the end moves a full step.
Carousel paging: a row that narrows while a finger holds it now rests where the row ends, instead of short of its end by as much as it narrowed.
Carousel paging: while the paging holds a row, the pager measures its pages and travel from the row's layout, as at rest.

Under snap paging, a Carousel's release bakes the settle's keyframes once, not once per item, and plays the settle only on the items that can show. With 9 items the release takes about a third less main-thread time, and with 30 items about two thirds less.

A `Step` keeps its own `aria-current` over a caller's. Before, an `aria-current` passed to a `Step` replaced the reflected value, so a step that was not in progress could be marked current and the in-progress step could lose `aria-current="step"`. Now only the in-progress step carries `aria-current="step"`, whatever the caller passes. No API changes.

Every import in an `astryx swizzle` copy now names a file the copy holds or a path the owner package exports. Before, the copy sent every import that left the component folder to the package's folder entry, which does not export the internal helpers most components use, so `Button`, `Dialog`, `Table` and about 100 other copies failed to type-check or bundle. Now the copy imports what the package exports from the package, carries every internal module it needs beside it in the package's folder layout, and copies the nested folders it imports (such as `Table`'s `plugins/`). Test helpers and notes are no longer copied. A helper an earlier swizzle wrote is reused when it is the same and is never replaced by a copy that carries it, even with `--overwrite`: a different one stays, and the new copy writes its own under a version-suffixed name. Swizzling the component whose folder holds that helper treats it as one of that component's own files, which `--overwrite` replaces. A private attribute owner module and the style modules it imports are the exception, as before: a changed copy fails the command without `--overwrite` and is replaced with it. Fixes #3506.

A swizzled component whose source imports another Astryx package's internal module, such as a Lab component that uses Core's gesture primitives, no longer imports that private path, except a StyleX module that package exports, which the copy keeps importing by that path because its identity is its path. Swizzle carries every other such module, and what it reaches, into the copy under a folder named after its package (for example `components/astryx/core/internal/touch.ts`); that package's public names are still imported from the package.

`astryx swizzle` reports the npm packages a copy imports, such as `d3-scale` for a chart, with the version range the owner package declares, so the copy builds once you install them. The `swizzle.copy` receipt lists them in `dependencies`, and the text output names them to install. Node's built-in modules and the owner package itself are not listed.

`astryx swizzle` writes an `astryx-swizzle.json` marker into an output folder it owns (one the copy creates, an empty one, or one it marked before), naming each package the folder's copies came from and its version. `@astryxdesign/build`'s Babel, PostCSS and Vite integrations, and `withAstryx()` under webpack, compile the copies under that folder below `astryx-theme`, so a theme's component overrides reach a swizzled component as they reach the package component. For a folder that already holds other files it writes no marker and says what it found and how to add the marker by hand; the `swizzle.copy` receipt reports this in a new optional `marker` field. Under Turbopack and with the stock StyleX plugins, a copy's styles still land above the theme. The marker is not listed among the copy's files.

Tab's docs show how to give a tab help text: anchor a `Tooltip` on the `Tab` through its ref, so the description lands on the tab, and put a decorative info `Icon` in `endContent`. `endContent` is documented as non-interactive: a button, link, or `InfoTip` inside it would nest a control inside the tab's button (#10732).

Tab's docs show how to run the selected indicator edge to edge in one strip: a nested `Theme` that takes the app's color mode, extends the app's theme and sets `insetInline: '0'` on the `tab-indicator` target, so other TabLists keep the default indicator. The override is best effort across releases.

Under a mouse, a key that cannot scroll a DateInput, TimeInput or DateTimeInput wheel, as Tab, no longer ends the wheel's key step. On a busy page, Tab right after an arrow key could commit the row the wheel was leaving.
Table's column settings plugin keeps its active columns in state. When the table re-renders on its own after a render React discards, such as a suspended transition, it shows the committed columns.
The `table-filter` template's link-style header actions set `minHeight: 0` with their auto height, so no minimum holds them taller than their text.
