Tables can window fixed-height flat data: pass `useTableRowsVirtualization({rowHeight, initialViewportHeight})` to `Table.virtualization`. Table keeps the complete data and row identity, mounts only the rows in its viewport plus a few overscan rows, keeps native table semantics with full-table row positions, keeps the focused row mounted, and falls back to rendering every row for content or geometry it cannot window. Tables that do not opt in are unchanged.

`Table`: three of its keyboard tab stops draw the theme's focus ring instead of the browser's default: the scroll wrapper once the table scrolls inline, and the tree plugin's row expander and expand-all toggle. A theme's `--focus-outline-*` tokens now reach them. The scroll wrapper's ring sits inside its box, clear of a bordered Card's border, so a Card no longer cuts off its edges (a Card's rounded corners still trim the ring's square corners); at `density="compact"` the tree toggles' ring sits inside the toggle, so the row does not clip it. The row-expansion, grouped-rows and filter buttons are unchanged.

The grouped table page template groups its rows with `useTableGroupedRows` instead of hand-rendered header rows and a hand-written `colgroup`. Its columns now have headers, each group's toggle is a button that reports whether its group is expanded, and the row menu's Move to project arrow mirrors in right-to-left.

`useTableRowsVirtualization`'s `viewportHeight` is renamed `initialViewportHeight` before the hook's first stable release. It only sizes the first window, on the server and before the viewport is measured; it no longer sets the Table's height. A windowed Table scrolls inside the height its parent gives it, so give the parent a height. `rowHeight` is unchanged.

Table: a row expansion panel with `panelVariant="muted"` now paints its wash on its cell, so with an `animatedLayout` handle the wash slides in with the panel's content. On iOS Safari the panel's edge trailed the rows gliding below it for a few frames; now they stay together. At rest the panel looks the same.

A Table column-resize handle now announces its column's rendered width from the first render after layout, and its announced range always holds that width, also when the layout renders a column past its maximum or minimum width. Before, until a column was first resized, its handle announced the column's minimum width, so a screen reader read the wrong width.

A Table column-resize handle on a column with no maximum width now announces a maximum at or above its value, so a screen reader no longer reads the width past ARIA's default maximum of 100. It uses the window's width as the stand-in maximum, as an unbounded Resizable region does, and announces its value in words, for example "133 pixels". A column with `maxWidth` is unchanged.

Table plugins can now read where a row sits. Table passes each body row and cell transform an immutable `TableRowContext` (the row's key, its zero-based `logicalIndex` in the complete data, the row and header counts, and the row model). It passes the scroll-wrapper transform a `TableRenderContext` with a stable `viewport` reference. A plugin declares `rowModel: 'flat'` when its body transforms keep one row per data item. `useTableSelection` and `useTableStickyColumns` declare it. `useTableRowIndex()` without options now numbers rows from the context (passing `data` still numbers from that array), and rows that move re-render only for plugins that read the index. Read context values during the transform; a later read from a callback warns in development. The CLI's numbered-rows block no longer passes `data`.
useTableRowIndex builds its number column once per plugin, so a parent re-render no longer re-renders every row of a table that shows row numbers.
A Table plugin's `transformScrollWrapper` className now reaches the table's scroll container beside the wrapper's own class; before, the wrapper replaced it.

`TableSelectionToolbar` documents how to select every row that matches a query across server pages with today's API: the app keeps "every matching row minus exclusions" and passes the toolbar its own count and label. In this mode the toolbar's `selectedKeys` holds only the loaded rows.

TableTree rows no longer carry `aria-expanded`, which is valid on a row only in a treegrid. Each row's expand and collapse button still exposes its expanded state, and rows keep `aria-level` for their depth.

A swizzled `Table` now honors `virtualization` from the package's `useTableRowsVirtualization`, and the package `Table` honors a capability from a swizzled copy. Before, each copy recognized only its own capability, so a swizzled Table rendered every row and its code failed to type-check. The capability is read through a registered, versioned key, and its type carries one required brand member that is never present at runtime, so only the hook makes a capability. A `virtualization` value the hook did not make now gets its own development warning. No API changes.

Windowed tables stay windowed with row selection and row numbers. A windowed row-number column widens to fit its last number before that row mounts, at the table's font and density, and pinned columns after it move with it.

`TabList` tabs, including a `TabMenu` tab, grow with a larger text size. Their size now sets a minimum height instead of a fixed one, so at 200% text and above a tab label is no longer clipped. At the default text size nothing changes.

The Tailwind guide (`astryx docs styling-libraries/tailwind`) adds a recipe for an app that already uses Tailwind: keep the app's own `@import "tailwindcss"`, put the `@layer` line above it, and add the Astryx stylesheets after it. It explains why the `@layer` line must come before the Tailwind import: below it, the Astryx reset outranks every utility class, and nothing reports it. The Core README's Next.js + Tailwind section points to it.

The `useInputStatusIcon — Coupon Code Status` example block's field applies `inputWrapperStyles.textField`. A field copied from it now shows its focus look at once when the primary pointer is coarse, as Core's text fields do.

`astryx template <name>` puts the template a typo slips from first in its suggestions: a name one or two slips away (a letter added, dropped or changed, or two letters swapped, as in `AppShellCotnentOnly` or `dasbhoard`) ranks just below the templates that carry every typed word. The suggestion list is never longer than before.

TextInput, TextArea, NumberInput, DateInput, DateRangeInput, DateTimeInput, TimeInput, Tokenizer, Typeahead, PowerSearch, ChatComposer and RichTextEditor: when the primary pointer is coarse (a phone or tablet), the focus look shows at once, with no fade, so a tapped field repaints once while the keyboard rises. With a fine primary pointer, such as a mouse, a click and the Tab key keep the fade. ChatComposer's focus depth also shows at once under reduced motion, as the other fields' focus look already does.

TextInput: the clear button now runs `changeAction` with the empty value and shows the optimistic empty value and busy state, as typing does. The clear goes through the input's own change handler, so `onChange` and `changeAction` receive a real change event (before, `onChange` received `null` as its event and `changeAction` did not run), `onChange` runs first, and its `preventDefault()` cancels the Action.

A truncated Text or Heading mounts its tooltip on the first hover, tap or focus, not as soon as it renders, so a long table or list of truncated cells mounts no closed tooltip layers at load. The hover delay, the tap and the focus rules are the tooltip's own: a touch that becomes a scroll opens nothing, and a tap outside closes it. No visual change.

Truncating Text and Heading take a newly mounted element's first measurement from the shared resize observer's first notification, after the browser's own layout, instead of forcing a layout pass after each commit. Pages and windowed tables that mount many truncating texts commit faster; the tooltip behaves as before.

Theming: a theme's `:active` override now follows the touch press model. With a mouse it still paints on `:active`. Under a finger it paints only while Astryx believes the press, so a themed control no longer flashes the theme's press color on the touch itself or while the page scrolls.

Theme packages publish the declarations of their `./theme.css` export. The export pointed `types` at `theme.css.d.ts`, which the package didn't ship, so TypeScript found no types for `import '@astryxdesign/theme-<name>/theme.css'`. The export is unchanged; the file is now published.

In Safari on iPhone, text follows the reader's text size (Dynamic Type) in every theme, branded included. Where the browser exposes that size through `font: -apple-system-body`, as Safari on iPhone does, the theme's font sizes scale with the size the reader picked in Settings (Display & Text Size, then Larger Text), each size on the curve of the iOS text style it plays: body text like Body, `heading-1` like Title 1, display text like Large Title, with every role kept in order. A semantic size a theme fixes at a length, such as the 0.75rem supporting text of Butter, Stone and Y2K, scales on the curve of the step it reads by default. At the default size every font size is the theme's own; the family, spacing, line-height ratios and the root font size never change, text inputs keep their 16px floor on iOS, and browsers without the keyword see no change. There is no option, prop or document attribute: the root `Theme` reads the reader's size from a hidden element. `astryx docs typography/type-scale` describes it.

Theme packages declare `"type": "module"`, so bundlers and Node read the `./built` entry as the ES module it is. Before, it was an ES module in a `.js` file in a package without a `type`, which tools that follow the package's `type` read as CommonJS. Every export subpath stays the same. The CommonJS build of the source entry is now `dist/source.cjs` behind the same `require` condition, with its own CommonJS declarations (`dist/source.d.cts`), so TypeScript types each condition in the format it loads. As before, `require('…/built')` loads an ES module, so it needs a Node version with `require(esm)` (22.12 or later). Deep imports that reach past `exports` into `dist/` change too: `dist/source.js` is now `dist/source.cjs`, and a `require` of `dist/<theme>.js` gets an ES module (`require(esm)`, Node 22.12 or later).
Matcha: light-mode secondary text is slightly darker (Neutral Light 30), so it meets 4.5:1 on the body (5.11:1, was 3.83:1), the surface and the card.
changesets.body:
[fix] Y2K: light-mode secondary text is slightly darker (Neutral Light 35), so it meets 4.5:1 on the Periwinkle body (5.14:1, was 4.25:1).
The CLI's Matcha and Y2K theme templates match.

changesets.headline: `Theme` keeps its runtime-injected CSS in the document until the last mounted `Theme` using that theme unmounts. Before, the `Theme` that injected the CSS first owned the shared `<style>` tags, so unmounting it (a nested `Theme` around a dialog that mounted first, for example) stripped the component overrides and prose defaults from every other `Theme` still using that theme. Built themes, which import their CSS as a file, are unaffected.

Replace the theme showcase's custom layout, text and icon styling with Astryx components. The embedded preview paints the theme's body behind card-token surfaces instead of a surface-colored card band. The new standalone top-navigation shell uses the theme's surface canvas; the embedded view stays shell-free. Make demo inputs, cart feedback, inventory filters and chat respond locally, with clearable filters and no payment submission. Keep the template id, gallery visibility and demo content.

The Butter, Stone and Y2K themes set supporting text (`--text-supporting-size`) in rem instead of a fixed 12px, so it grows when a reader raises the browser's default font size, like the rest of the text. At the default size it is still 12px. The CLI's copies of these themes match.

`TimeInput` shows the stepped time after an arrow-key adjustment made while a typed draft is pending, and leaving the field keeps that step. Before, the text typed before pressing ArrowUp or ArrowDown stayed in the box while the committed value and the screen-reader announcement had moved on, and blurring re-parsed that stale text and committed it over the step, silently undoing it.

Timer hardening pass (Layers 1–2 of the Component Hardening Protocol, #6483). No behavior defect found — the audit confirmed the tick pipeline, format ladder, cadence switch, and resource cleanup match the `spec:AST-037` contract. Two untested guards are now pinned: the wait for a distant future `startTime` is capped at the 32-bit `setTimeout` ceiling, and an unknown `format` value coerces to `elapsed`. The Default story now asserts in a real browser that the display advances on its own. (#6483)
Timestamp exposes its details popup on the focusable time element.

Toast: the viewport is each toast's only announcement owner. While an open modal hosts a top-layer viewport (the default), it announces each toast through that modal's own live regions, so a toast shown over a Dialog is announced once. Elsewhere it announces through the shared channel. A viewport rendered in place announces through `useAnnounce`, which delivers inside an enclosing Astryx modal. The toast card is no longer a live region inside a viewport, including while a modal hosts it.

Under the touch presentation, ToggleButtonGroup tracks a finger's or a pen's press across its toggles, like a menu. Press a toggle and slide across the others: the highlight follows, and only the toggle you lift on changes. Lifting outside the group changes nothing. A mouse press is unchanged: it acts as a native toggle's, on the toggle it began on. With a finger, a toggle the group tracks keeps its 44 px target, now drawn by the group. A toggle without a value keeps its own press, and the keyboard is unchanged. Before, each toggle tracked only its own press, and sliding off it changed nothing. An enabled ToggleButtonGroup root is position: relative under a coarse pointer, so absolutely positioned children anchor to the group. With a fine primary pointer, the group is unchanged.

Tokenizer forwards `cancel` to its `searchSource`, so a newer search, closing the menu or the sheet, focus leaving the field, or unmounting cancels the consumer's in-flight search (for example, to abort its request). Previously the inline field wrapped the source to filter selected items and dropped `cancel`, and the bottom-sheet presentation never called it.

A `Toolbar` with `centerContent` wraps its row when its lanes don't fit, as at a larger text size on a phone, instead of letting the center title spill over the buttons beside it and past the screen's edge. The end lane, and the center lane when it does not fit beside the start lane, move to a following line. The center sits at the toolbar's middle as before while each side lane fits in half of the width it leaves. In a narrow container, a center `TabList` now shows all its tabs and the row wraps, and its tabs scroll only when they are wider than the toolbar.

A controlled `Tooltip` held closed (`isOpen={false}`) no longer opens on keyboard focus or a click into a text-field trigger. It reports that focus as `onOpenChange(true)` and shows nothing, so the caller decides, the same way Escape on a held-open tooltip reports `onOpenChange(false)` without hiding. Before, focus opened a held-closed tooltip anyway, and Escape could not close it. `useTooltip` reports the same focus through `onShow` under `isOpen={false}`.

on a touch screen, keys typed into a text field no longer make the focus a closing dialog returns to a Tooltip or HoverCard trigger open its layer; Tab, Escape and arrow keys still count as keyboard input. `useTouchTrigger`'s `isTouchInteraction()` from `@astryxdesign/core/Layer` stays true in that case too. A field in an iframe or Picture-in-Picture window is not read as a text-entry field, so typing there still opens the tooltip as before (#9464)

A disabled `TopNavItem` now keeps its Tab stop, in both the bar and the drawer. Before, it rendered with `tabIndex={-1}`, so Tab skipped it and keyboard and screen-reader users could not reach it. Now it is a focusable `link` that exposes `aria-disabled="true"`, while a click, Enter or Space still runs no `onClick` or `onKeyDown`, does not navigate, and does not close the mobile drawer (`spec:AST-085` FR1, FR2, FR5, `TopNavItem` FR3). No API changes.

TopNav's heading can now shrink, so a heading wider than the whole bar ends in an ellipsis instead of running off the bar and scrolling the page sideways (#9530). `TopNavHeading` keeps its logo whole, and independently linked lines wrap and keep their longest word; a plain line beside them still keeps its full width.

`TopNav` wraps its bar when its regions don't fit one row, as at a larger text size, instead of letting the end content (such as buttons) cover the navigation items. The end content moves to a second line. While the regions fit, the bar and its centered content look as before.

DateInput's touch sheet keeps keyboard focus when the month reaches the end of the range, by an arrow press or a swipe, while a month arrow holds focus. That arrow hides there, so focus now moves first to the other month arrow, or to the month-and-year button when both arrows hide. Before, focus fell to the page.

Under a coarse primary pointer, expanding a `TreeList` row glides the rows below it to their new places on the shared layout glide while its children fade in on the same timing, so the tree moves as one. A collapse fades the children out as the rows below glide up, and the chevron turns on that timing. The rows used to appear and leave in a single frame. Without an `animatedLayout` handle the motion stays inside the tree, so content after the tree takes its place at once, and the tree clips its bottom edge while it moves so no row paints over that content; pass a handle for it to glide too. The guide lines beside a group now show and hide with its rows. With reduced motion on and a finger, the children fade in where they land. With a mouse the rows still change at once. Under every pointer, a guide line now ends at the last row it joins instead of running on beside an expanded last row's children.

BaseTypeahead takes `menu`, which chooses what its anchored menu shows while Astryx keeps the layer: its position, top layer, outside press, Escape, focus return and ARIA. `{role: 'listbox', render}` places information such as a header or a key hint around the result list, and anything a person acts on stays a result, so the arrow keys reach it (a control outside the list warns in development). `{role: 'dialog', label, render}` shows content that takes focus in a dialog named by `label`; closing it returns focus to the element focused when it opened, or to the input. A new `handleRef` exposes `open()` and `close()`, and `onOpenChange` reports each change; there is no controlled open state. Calling `open()` from `onChange` keeps the menu open, so a pick can switch the list to a dialog on the same layer. Typeahead forwards `menu` and `handleRef`.

Toast: the `useToast` fallback warning and its server-rendering error no longer tell you to wrap the app in `<AppShell>`. AppShell provides no layer context, so that advice left the warning in place. They now name only `<LayerProvider>`, which removes it.

With a mouse or trackpad, a date or time sheet's wheel no longer turns back to the row a key step is leaving. A key step commits its row at once and then scrolls there. On a busy page or a slow device the scroll could draw no frame for longer than the wheel's quiet period, or the browser could end it part-way, and the wheel took that pause for rest: it committed the row under the band and turned back there. A rest before the step's row is reached now finishes the scroll instead. A scroll a person makes still rests where it stops.
